response.guide:
How to interpret the response:
- result.scan_id — the created scan (or, when scan_id was passed, that same scan: the update landed as a new configuration version on it). Pass this to run_scan, update_scan_filters, or update_scan_config in follow-up calls.
- result.scan_title — final title (custom if provided; else Beacon's default for a new scan, or the existing title on a scan_id update).
- result.filters_applied — the filter set actually in effect after the call. If this doesn't match what the user asked for, one of the composite steps failed silently — surface that to the user.
- result.results — initial live results (real-time market data at scan creation time).
- result.total_items — total matches. May exceed len(results) if the scan's frontend_limit is hit.

When presenting:
- Confirm the scan was created and note its title + filters_applied (so the user knows what was actually saved).
- Render the initial results as a table.
- Tell the user the scan is saved and can be re-run anytime with run_scan + the returned scan_id.
- If results is empty: tell the user no instruments match the filters right now, and suggest broadening them with update_scan_filters.

Error handling:
- "unknown preset X" → preset enum not recognized. List the valid presets to the user.
- "filter[N]: ..." → filter validation failure at index N. Tell the user which filter and why. Rejected before any Beacon call — nothing was created.
- "created by Cortex and cannot be modified" (with scan_id) → the target scan is Cortex-managed. Offer to create a fresh scan (omit scan_id) instead.
- "column X already exists from a filter" → one of the scan's filters already produces a column with that display name, and an expression was passed for it as well. Re-send that column with NO expression to customize it (visibility, position), or give it a different display_name. Do not drop the filter.
- "no standard column is named X" → the display name is not a standard column and no expression was given. Pick one of the valid names the error lists, or supply an expression from get_scanner_datapoints.
- Partial-failure responses (e.g. "scan X created but preset Y could not be applied") indicate a partial success on the enum path: the scan exists but is missing some of the intended state. Use filters_applied on the response to see what actually landed; mention this clearly to the user so they know whether they need to follow up with update_scan_filters.
- With expression filters there are no partial failures: an upstream validation error (e.g. "unresolved reference: X", "unsupported candle-period") means nothing was saved. Fix the expression — get_scanner_datapoints has the valid names and signatures — and call again, or iterate with preview_scan first.
